I took my two miniature schnauzers here for almost a year, and unfortunately, after several issues, I’ve decided not to bring them back.

Both of my dogs get slightly different haircuts, and there have been multiple times when I clearly explained what I wanted but the cuts came out differently than requested. The last time we went, the person at the front desk even took a photo of the exact haircut one of my dogs was supposed to receive. Somehow, the dog who was supposed to get that haircut didn’t get it, while my other dog did. They essentially got the two dogs mixed up, which was frustrating and concerning.

My biggest concern, however, came up today. I had noticed that one of my dog’s nails had gotten extremely long and was starting to hook onto things like the couch, so I took her to our vet to have them trimmed. The vet told us that, based on the length of her nails, it appeared they had not been properly trimmed in around six months. They actually recommended that we find a different groomer. Considering we had been regularly taking both dogs in for grooming, this was really upsetting to hear.

There have also been some communication issues throughout the year. At our last appointment, we were charged an additional fee for a “specialty haircut” because they are miniature schnauzers. I completely understand if a certain cut costs more, but we had been going there for nearly a year and had never been charged that additional fee before, so the sudden change was confusing.

The staff has always seemed friendly, and I don’t like leaving negative reviews, but after everything that has happened, especially what our vet told us about the nails, I felt like I should share our experience. When you leave your dogs with a groomer, you’re trusting that they’re receiving proper care even when you aren’t there to see it. Between the repeated haircut mix-ups, communication issues, and now finding out that my dog’s nails apparently had not been properly trimmed for months, I no longer feel comfortable bringing my dogs here.

I just wanted other pet owners to be aware of our experience when deciding where to take their dogs.

I’m extremely disappointed with the grooming service I received. I paid $90 expecting professional care, but the results were far from acceptable. My poodle’s clips were uneven, her ears were cut crooked, and her tail wasn’t brushed or properly fluffed at all. On top of that, she came home covered in short, loose fur from the haircut, which shows a lack of proper finishing and cleanup.

What’s even more concerning is how poorly her nails were handled. They were left terribly sharp to the point that they cut my skin on the drive home.

It was clear one of her quicks had been cut too short, as they were bloody when she was returned to me. Even worse, no one informed me this had happened, which is completely unacceptable. That’s not just careless—it’s unsafe, painful for my dog, and a serious lack of transparency.

First visit to Doggy Daze in January 2025 was a great experience. My Schnoxie came back to me clean, fluffed and lookin' REALLY good.
However, a good groomer, for me, is more than how a pet looks. It's also about how they are treated. This is the reason I'll no longer return there. 2nd visit was 180° turnaround. Besides a very disappointing groom (poor cut, untouched face and underbelly, and no Teddy Bear look SO unlike the 1st time), I found his nails had not been smoothed, so I asked to have it done. While waiting, I wandered back to the little gated  room where Monti was waiting to get that additional service and watched him through the window. That's when I saw a large young man reach over the gate grabbing Monti by the back of his neck, roughly drag him into the closed gate and lift him into his arms. The man turned Monti onto his back squeezing him into a position where he struggled but couldn't move while another guy took his feet to grind his nails. By time I got around to the area where I had direct access to where they held my boy, obviously frightened and attemptimg to bite his way to freedom, they'd forced a muzzle on him. At that point, I demanded the large man release Monti to me, and confronted him on his mistreatment of the animal. My complaint was VERY CLEARLY, expressed to the front desk individual as well.
It appeared that the young people involved in this incident where not, by any stretch of the imagination, trained in appropriate handling of those animals in their care and trusted by pet parents not to be mistreated.
Having to leave such a detailed, negative review is unfortunate, but perhaps it will help the next Doggy Daze client be aware of what happens behind the scenes of this place.
